  - 3-4: d = +0.46 (τ = 0.47)
  - 4-5: d = +0.25
  - 2-3-4: d = +0.42
  - 4-5-6: d = +0.25
- No nonadjacent set can contain two of the top consecutive frames, so these matches are one-sided by construction. The rule τ = 0.2·|m| still allows a gap of about 0.4 nat.    - blur adjacent 1-2 has I = +0.42 at m = 0.25;
   - blur 5-6-7 has I = +0.36 at m = 0.46;
   - nonconsecutive 3-5-7 has I = +0.42 at m = 1.20, but 0-4-7 has I = −0.15 at m = 1.39.
   
   The "saturation" is not consistent either: all-eight I is −0.91 in blur but +0.90 in constant, at about the same m. The data do not show a clean convex response in m.
